messages:
maria: heads-up — vuln-bot ingested a small batch from the OSS RPM feed, need quick intake and scoring. hits: CVE-2026-3452 (libssl), CVE-2026-4001 (rpm-tooling), CVE-2026-4102 (libcurl). full bot output below.

sec-bot: automated alert: 3 new vulns affecting our RPM inventory. metadata: CVE-2026-3452 CVSS=9.8 EPSS=0.78, CVE-2026-4001 CVSS=6.1 EPSS=0.12, CVE-2026-4102 CVSS=7.5 EPSS=0.44. Suggested owners: infra/agents, infra/packaging, telemetry.

maria: quick ask — exploit proof-of-concept observed for CVE-2026-3452? EPSS high but want human check.

devon: I pulled the advisory. 3452 is a classic RL buffer overread in TLS handshake parsing. PoC exists in public repo but requires crafted client. low/no internet worm curve but high impact if telemetry agent talks to untrusted endpoints.

oliver: confirming telemetry agent (agentd) links against libssl. list of hosts with vulnerable package: ~120 dedicated nodes + staging pools.

maria: ok. priority from my POV: CVE-2026-3452 = P0 (hotfix), CVE-2026-4102 = P1 (schedule), CVE-2026-4001 = P2. Thoughts?

devon: +1 on P0 for libssl. mitigation options: emergency backport to our stable build or temporary firewall rules to block client-initiated TLS to untrusted hosts from agent namespace.

sara: can we do a canary rollout to dedicated pool first? we should also confirm ksm/KMS client libs not affected — KMS calls use TLS via libcurl on some paths. if libcurl is impacted (4102) we may need to treat it as P0 for KMS clients.

oliver: I ran a grep across repos: only kms-client and agentd use libcurl directly. kms-client talks to keyservice over mTLS using client certs, so PoC exploitation unlikely without MITM, but still risk.

maria: action items —
- devon: validate PoC on isolated VM and produce quick repro steps (deadline: +6h)
- oliver: inventory all hosts with libssl/libcurl versions and mark owners (deadline: +3h)
- sara: check KMS access logs for anomalies in past 72h and flag suspicious flows (deadline: +4h)

devon: repro snippet (isolated env):
```bash
# build minimal PoC container
docker run --rm -it --name poc -v $(pwd):/mnt alpine:3.18 /bin/sh
# inside: fetch PoC and compile
apk add build-base openssl-dev git
git clone https://example.com/poc-3452.git && cd poc-3452 && make
./poc-client --target <our-staging-ip>
```
will redact specifics in the intel doc.

sec-bot: note: EPS S threshold 0.5 used for auto-priority bump to P0 for any CVSS>=9.0 + EPSS>=0.5. manual override allowed.

maria: thanks. devon — if PoC runs in isolated VM, write short runbook and include suggested mitigations (CVE KB entry + urgency). put that in #vuln-knowledgebase.

oliver: inventory query posted to infra-assets channel: `rpm -q --queryformat "%{NAME} %{VERSION}-%{RELEASE} %{EPOCH}\n" openssl libcurl | sed -n '1,200p'`. will attach CSV shortly.

sara: audit log check — running splunk search: `index=kms logs sourcetype=kms_access earliest=-72h | stats count by src_ip,action` currently running. I'll post findings.

maria: RBAC check: if we push hotfix to kms-client we need staged deploy with role restriction so only kube-system deployers can apply. @oliver add gating to rollout policy.

oliver: noted — I'll add a canary gate and require sign-off from sec before global rollout. also adding preflight smoke test that exercises KMS operations.

devon: short-term mitigation suggestion: add iptables rule on agentd namespace to disallow outbound TLS to untrusted IP ranges (config managed in infra-policy). low risk, reversible.

maria: thanks team. summary/next: P0 = CVE-2026-3452 (libssl) — hold patch window tonight, canary to 10% dedicated pool, rollback plan ready. P1 = CVE-2026-4102 (libcurl) — monitor impact and schedule for next maintenance. P2 = CVE-2026-4001 (rpm-tooling) — patch in weekly. owners assigned as above. we'll reconvene after PoC + inventory. :white_check_mark:

sec-bot: followup reminder scheduled in 6h.
